title: Fixed Split Crown and Curled Tine Bamboo Tea Whisk
description: One newly authored complete static chasen-inspired bamboo tea-whisk appearance. A short whole bamboo-look handle has a real blind lower hollow and a finite annular resting sole. Its upper solid neck roots twenty complete slender flat outer tines which flare outward, rise and curl inward at their open tips; twelve whole inner single-root tines form a separate inward-narrowing crown. One full fixed annular binding sits around the neck and outer roots. Every tine has finite tapered width and thickness with closed end faces, not an alpha fibre or loose line. The real radial and circumferential gaps between the inner crown and flared outer crown are open geometry. All numerical handle, root, two distinct crown paths, taper and binding are newly authored together. Unlike the long metal balloon whisk with returned loops rooted at both ends into an axial ferrule, these are individual open-ended flat strips from a short upright base; unlike a scrub brush, there is no flat brush back, downward tuft field or overhead grip. Thirty-four closed editable whole meshes, four opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and whole horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. One complete model zero scenes; tines are not separate assets. Broad Japanese tea-utensil category artwork only, not a named artisan object, tea-school specification, exact tine count, authentic bamboo construction or historic replica. Components remain editable closed visual solids with hidden finite root overlaps; no claim of carving all pieces from one real bamboo stem or reproducing woven thread topology. No tea, food preparation, whisking/frothing performance, food-contact suitability, actual bamboo species/fibres, flex, comfort, washing, manufacture, stability or safety capability. No rig, animation or interaction.
